$scope: The 4 `icons/resource-*` assets visible in review/compare/compare-icons.png (aether, cloudstone, provisions, skysteel), scored beside their counterparts. A SAMPLE, not the whole icons set — stated so the counts are not read as out of 25. NOTE the third column is a DIFFERENT PROMPT DIALECT — see COMPARISON.md's positive-dialect section — scored on the same four assets and the same taxonomy, which is what makes it readable, but it is not a controlled comparison with the first two and must not be read as one.

$notes.the shape of the error: Qwen read every one as a mobile-game ITEM CARD — decorative frame, bevelled centre panel, lighter background — rather than as a flat icon on the ash ground. The subject is right every time (aether droplet, cloudstone, wheat sheaf, skysteel ingot); it is the artefact type that is wrong, which is why criterion 1's arithmetic largely passes it and the eye does not.
$notes.qwen-image-2512-positive: 4 of 4 framed and 4 of 4 bevelled, against a brief carrying no prohibition words at all. The item-card reading survived the rewrite intact: decorative border, bevelled centre panel, lighter inner field. It got WORSE in two places the literal set had right — resource-aether returned a large blue arc instead of a teardrop above a ring, and resource-skysteel returned a plain cube instead of a notched ingot, so 'idea not recognisable' goes from 0 of 4 to 2 of 4. The one clause that moved is the one about the field behind the subject: aether and skysteel came back on a mottled brown texture, which is worse than the literal set's flat dark panels.

$pilot.$scope: This repository's contribution to the estate-wide 15-asset positive-dialect pilot, micro-brand/COMPARISON.md section 9.3. These are the same 4 `icons/resource-*` assets the columns above score, restated under the row names that section's table uses, so the three repositories' contributions can be summed without a name-matching step. The other 11 are micro-brand's 2 currency marks and emberkin's 9 `types` icons. claims.py sums the three $pilot blocks, checks each one against the columns it was taken from via $columnAlias, and checks the section 9.3 table against the sum.

$columnAlias.non-flat (3D, bevel, gradient, glow): non-flat rendering (3D, bevel, gradient, glow, texture)
$columnAlias.ground not the flat ash field: ground not the flat ash field
$columnAlias.idea not recognisable from the plan: idea not recognisable from the plan

$unscored.construction guides drawn: Not scored over the icons sheet by this reviewer, so there is no figure to sum and claims.py does not pin that row of the section 9.3 table.
$unscored.recognisable pastiche of an existing art: Not scored here either. The absence is recorded rather than filled with a zero: an unscored row and a row scored zero are different statements, and only one of them is evidence.
